name: Orthonormal discrete Hartley transform
definition: H_k=N^(−1/2) Σ_(n=0)^(N−1) x_n [cos(2πkn/N)+sin(2πkn/N)]; x_n=N^(−1/2) Σ_(k=0)^(N−1) H_k [cos(2πkn/N)+sin(2πkn/N)].
variables: N positive integer length; n,k indices; x real input and H real coefficients
assumptions: Finite real vector and symmetric normalization
limitations: Equivalent information to the real-input DFT; direct evaluation is quadratic; not a claim of faster runtime
computation: Evaluate real kernel sums directly; inverse uses the same kernel.

name: Prime-field number theoretic transform
definition: For prime p and N dividing p−1, choose ω of exact order N in F_p; X_k=Σ_(n=0)^(N−1)x_n ω^(nk) mod p; x_n=N^(−1) Σ_(k=0)^(N−1)X_k ω^(−nk) mod p.
variables: p prime modulus; N positive integer length; ω primitive Nth root; N^(−1) modular inverse
assumptions: Finite-field inputs; N divides p−1; exact order N verified
limitations: Modular residues do not directly recover unrestricted integer coefficients; requires appropriate modulus and arithmetic
computation: Evaluate modular sums and inverse using modular exponentiation; no fast implementation claimed.
application: General finite-field transformation; no forecasting benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Prime modulus, vector, root of exact order N
incompatible_methods: Arbitrary complex-valued inputs without a specified mapping
